options.reason: The table is a transactional retail log with no column usable as a supervised outcome (Quantity and UnitPrice are per-line magnitudes, not row-level labels), so the evident purpose is segmenting customers into behavioral groups from Recency/Frequency/Monetary-style aggregates built from InvoiceDate, Quantity and UnitPrice. CustomerID is the repeating source unit, so its rows must be aggregated and kept in one partition; timestamps are only used to build static recency features, so no time columns are declared.
options.title: clustering

options.reason: If the scientific aim is to forecast per-line order quantity, Quantity is the single numeric outcome and UnitPrice is a co-recorded price known alongside the outcome, excluded as a leakage-risk feature. CustomerID groups rows so customers are not split across splits.
options.title: regression
